c.tagline: Northern gateway on the Nan River, home to Thailand's most revered Buddha.

taxi.fareNote: There are few metered street taxis; getting around means flagging a shared songthaew truck or a tuk-tuk and agreeing the short-hop fare (roughly 15-40 baht per person) before you ride, or booking a Grab car. Cycle samlors still ferry passengers short distances near the market.

emergency.note: Tourist Police 1155 has English-speaking operators; 191 reaches police and 1669 the ambulance/medical service.

hood_landmark.Nai Mueang (City Center / Riverside): Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat Phitsanulok
hood_landmark.Wat Chan: Wat Chan Tawantok Nan River Phitsanulok
hood_landmark.Aranyik: Sergeant Major Thawee Folk Museum Phitsanulok

hood_desc: The compact heart of Phitsanulok along the east bank of the Nan River, home to the revered Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) and its Phra Buddha Chinnarat image, the riverside night bazaar, and most of the city's hotels; best for first-timers who want everything walkable.
The west-bank district across the Nan River, a quieter, mostly residential and local-market area with floating riverside restaurants and easy access back over the bridges to the center.

A northern district known for the Sergeant Major Thawee Folk Museum and the Buranathai Buddha Image Foundry, where the famous Chinnarat replicas are cast; more spread-out, local and craft-focused in feel.
The eastern university quarter around Naresuan University, with student cafes, cheap eateries and a youthful, budget-friendly atmosphere away from the tourist core.
A southern residential and academic fringe near Naresuan University's health-sciences campus and Bueng Phra lake, quiet and green with budget guesthouses.
lodging: The Imperial Hotel & Convention Centre Phitsanulok

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not reliably potable.

transit.pay: Pay songthaews and tuk-tuks in cash directly to the driver — around 15-30 baht per person for short hops in town, agreed before you ride; there is no rechargeable transit card system.
transit.hours: Songthaews, tuk-tuks and cycle samlors run through the day and into the evening, thinning out at night when Grab fills the gap.
transit.note: Phitsanulok has no metro, tram, or urban rail transit; getting around the compact center means songthaew shared trucks, a few local bus routes, tuk-tuks and ride-hailing via Grab, with the classic three-wheeled samlor still working the streets near the market.

bus: Phitsanulok Bus Terminal 2 (intercity coaches to Bangkok, Chiang Mai and Sukhothai)

car.idp: Required (International Driving Permit needed alongside your home license)

train: Phitsanulok Railway Station (State Railway of Thailand northern line, Bangkok–Chiang Mai via Ayutthaya)

transit.m: Airport taxi or Grab to the city center (10-15 min)
Free or low-cost shuttle offered by some central hotels

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill or leaving 20-40 baht for good service at restaurants is appreciated but not required.
